intro.author: Unknown. The writer never gives a name. Some in the early church linked it to Paul, but others doubted this from early on; suggestions include Barnabas, Apollos and Luke. The writer knew Timothy (13:23).
intro.written: Many scholars date it before AD 70, since it speaks of sacrifices as still being offered and never mentions the temple's destruction; others date it somewhat later
intro.audience: Believers, very likely Jewish Christians, who knew the Old Testament well; the greeting from 'they of Italy' (13:24) suggests a link to Italy, perhaps Rome
intro.setting: The readers had once endured public insult, imprisonment of friends and the seizure of their property (10:32-34), though none had yet died for the faith (12:4). Now some were growing weary and in danger of drifting back from their confession of Christ. The writer calls the work a 'word of exhortation' (13:22); it reads like a sermon with a letter's ending.
intro.purpose: To show that Jesus is greater than angels, Moses and the Levitical priesthood, that his one sacrifice fulfills the old covenant, and to urge readers to hold fast to him.
intro.bigIdea: Jesus is God's final word and our great high priest, so hold fast to him and do not drift away.

outline.title: Greater than Moses; the promised rest
A better covenant and a better sacrifice

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE HEBREWS
